decisions.reason: After four years the market has mostly revealed this classic handle line's value, but as a close-to-core and relatively low-cost range it is still worth retaining unless internal overlap becomes too great.

This handle family sits squarely in the firm's established assortment, so despite reduced uncertainty the firm would usually keep it while it continues to support breadth across projects and price points.
By now project feedback should be sufficient, and as a single handle design rather than a broader family it has less remaining option value and is the easiest candidate to prune.
Because this family extends assortment breadth in a familiar category with limited ongoing risk, the firm would likely keep it unless sales evidence clearly trails competing in-house lines.
As a flagship electronic access system aligned with the firm's digital building direction, it still offers strategic upside that justifies keeping it despite higher carrying and support costs.
